source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus publishes 36 MW of IT load across three buildings, the fourth-largest disclosed figure in Texas, but its certifications point to regulated enterprise workloads rather than AI training.

The campus covers SAT2, SAT3 and SAT4, with 295,785 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a density used for AI training, 36 MW works out to roughly 900 racks. That is a small rack count for a footprint this size, which suggests the published figure describes what is built rather than what the site could hold. The record lists no announced expansion, and the suitability score of 68 is computed only from published IT capacity and operator type.

Texas is what limits how far this number can be read. Only 19 of the 133 mapped facilities in the state publish a capacity figure, and the 475 MW they total is a fraction of what the state hosts. Ranking fourth at 7.6% of that disclosed total measures how few operators publish specifications, not how important this campus is to AI scaling.

What is missing matters more than what is present. Power availability, grid interconnection and on-site generation are not published, so nothing here shows whether the site can draw the power its 36 MW implies. The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942, qualify the campus for finance, healthcare and federal workloads, and say nothing about GPU density, cooling or network fabric. The record also carries no street address and no coordinates, so proximity to transmission or substations cannot be checked.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
